patches.title: 42.20.4 STABLE & 42.19.2 UNSTABLE & 41.78.21 LEGACY Hotfixes Released
patches.content: While this update should not break saves, if you encounter any bugs please ensure you can replicate them on a fresh save with no mods installed before reporting them to our team here. FIXES Fixed security vulnerabilities. Mod makers should be aware that as part of this fix, the loadstring and loadstream methods have been removed. If your mods used these methods you will need to update your mods. If you were using these methods to execute code sent from the server, then you will need to create the necessary methods and call them by sending the appropriate commands. If you are unable to replace these methods in your case, please report the issue in the #mod_portal channel of The Official Project Zomboid Discord server, explaining how you were using them As always, discussions regarding this update can be found pinned to the Project Zomboid Discussions Forums here.

patches.title: 42.20.3 STABLE Hotfix Released
patches.content: While this update should not break saves, if you encounter any bugs please ensure you can replicate them on a fresh save with no mods installed before reporting them to our team here. MP Improved server player limit handling, including support for up to 254 players and administrator access when servers are full Fixed an issue that would cause the client to hang on "Loading Map" forever FIXES Addressed multiple causes of a memory leak that could lead to performance degradation and crashes over time If you continue to encounter an out of memory error in a new save, please submit a bug report with your logs and profiler video from debug so the team can investigate Implemented several memory optimisations Reduced instances of black and gray boxes appearing when travelling quickly through the world Additional causes of this issue are still being investigated and will be addressed in a future update Fixed issues that could cause errors during lighting updates. As always, discussions regarding this update can be found pinned to the Project Zomboid Discussions Forums here.

patches.title: 42.20.2 STABLE Hotfix Released
patches.content: While this update should not break saves, if you encounter any bugs please ensure you can replicate them on a fresh save with no mods installed before reporting them to our team here. TECHNICAL/DEBUG Fixed percent symbol handling in files Mods should use %% to display % characters A temporary workaround was implemented to allow both methods of processing, however mod makers should update their mods to use %% to display % characters going forward as this workaround will be removed in a future unstable update Error logs will be populated highlighting the error so mod makers can see what needs to be updated going forward Fixed quick tips displaying % as %% Added memory debug-information when showing fps debug info As always, discussions regarding this update can be found pinned to the Project Zomboid Discussions Forums here.

patches.title: 42.20.1 STABLE Hotfix Released
patches.content: While this update should not break saves, if you encounter any bugs please ensure you can replicate them on a fresh save with no mods installed before reporting them to our team here. MP Improved Lua checksum validation for multiplayer anti-cheat Fixed an issue that caused significant performance problems with chunk unloading on multiplayer servers This should fix most of the bugs players were getting on high-pop servers due to server lag Fixed errors and crashes that could occur when selecting Multiplayer while certain languages were selected Fixed an issue where vehicles could temporarily disappear for players after another player disconnected Fixed an issue that would allow broken B41 worlds to be hosted on B42 servers Fixed an issue where players switching from b41 to B42 could be met with a missing menu FIXES Improved memory usage by reusing discarded world data Fixed a memory leak that could lead to performance degradation and crashes over time If you continue to encounter an out of memory error in a new save, please submit a bug report with your logs and profiler video from debug so the team can investigate Fixed a rare exception that could occur during exploration TECHNICAL/DEBUG Added the ability for mods to write .json files Fixed percent symbol handling in translation files Mod translations should use %% to display % characters As always, discussions regarding this update can be found pinned to the Project Zomboid Discussions Forums here.

patches.title: Build 42.20.0 Stable Released
patches.content: As part of our preparations for the release of Build 42 Stable, we've also released a small security patch for Builds 41 and 42.19. We'd like to thank Jorge Escabias for responsibly disclosing this vulnerability and bringing it to our attention before it could be exploited. We greatly appreciate the time and effort involved in reporting issues like this, which helps us keep the game secure for everyone. There is a small chance this change may affect some mods. If you encounter any compatibility issues after the update, we would ask that mod authors please report them in the mod_portal channel on our Discord so we can investigate. How do I switch back to Build 41? Right-click PZ in your Steam library. Select "Properties". Under "Game Version & Betas" select "legacy41". B42 Feature List The patch notes below cover the changes between 42.19 and 42.20. For an overview of the features and additions introduced between Build 41 and Build 42, check out our feature list here. Please note that Build 42 has seen an enormous number of changes throughout development, so this should be considered a highlights overview rather than a complete list. NEW Map Glowup: Many area across the map have received a substantial overhaul from the mapping team Added a plethora of new tiles, buildings, and locations for these areas and elsewhere Implemented performance optimizations surrounding these new areas and features Various new room definitions and containers have been added and adjusted across a wide range of locations Added "Extra Large" Tree Types: XL and XXL trees and updated worldgen biomes to include them "Wood" loot generated by cutting down trees increased for Extra Large trees XL tree overhang can be hidden using right-click when driving or scouting ahead Challenge Mode Revamp: Two New Challenge Modes replace "Cabin in the Woods" in rotation: "28 Minutes Later" and "Top of the World" Adjusted spawn coordinates for "Winter is Coming" and "A Really CDDA" challenge modes Removed the ability to respawn in "A Really CDDA" challenge Challenge Modes menu UI videos and descriptions updated Updated the Main Menu artwork Main menu SFX is temporarily disabled Added epilepsy warning scree...

patches.title: 42.20: The Big Glow Up
patches.content: Hi everyone, as previously mentioned Build 42.20 will be coming to the public stable branch this Wednesday, July 29th! For full details on this please check out this announcement blog. A big new part of this is a HUGE new upgrade to the Knox Event Exclusion Zone – that goes way beyond what you have already played during the Unstable beta. Our aim? To create a heavily evolved Knox Country that expands and overhauls the game’s Kentucky setting with new and reworked areas, that feel more lived-in, more natural, and more believable as places that existed long before everything went wrong. So what’s got us to this point? Let’s hand over to Art Director Ayrton Orio to explain: “Since Build 41 the Art Department has been hard at work on expanding the map westward, establishing an ambitious target quality, and revamping many of the existing towns in-game – while also hiring and restructuring.” “Overall Build 42 in the Knox Event Art Department saw four new map artists added to the team (Erika, Melo, Dylan and Alokin), one departure (Xeonyx), two ascensions to wider game management positions (Mash and Binky), and my own promotion to Art Director.“ “The first improvements made to the map itself are those that Build 42 Unstable players have already experienced. Myself and Jamie (Xeonyx) made a first leg of improvement that covered a whole new area furnishing the extreme West of the map with three new towns: Brandenburg, a new location on the banks of the Ohio river river; Ekron, a small agricultural town full of Southern charm; and Irvington, in the South West of the map, with its famous race track.” "While we were working on the above, however, the South of Muldraugh became our proving ground to experiment on a much more detailed style of world building. If reception was positive, we thought, then this could eventually become the expected standard for the rest of the map.“ “As it turned out, the reaction from players when B42 hit Unstable was so overwhelmingly positive that it triggered the hiring of the new enlarged team mentioned above – which would then go on to achieve that vision we’re announcing today.” A snowy night in Muldraugh WHAT'S NEWFollowing on from Ayrton’s...

patches.title: BUILD 42 STABLE PLANS
patches.content: Project Zomboid version 42.20 will be coming direct to the stable public branch Wednesday, the 29th of July. Details on what this will entail will follow after, by way of celebration, the unveiling of our new Build 42 Steam Store trailer! This has been lovingly crafted by our Art Director Ayrton, captured by Amz, been blessed with 3D renders by Werlias, and received much sound love from Matteo and the team from Arrival. Our thanks too to our voice talent Michael Billington, Gemma Acosta, Jane Perry and Stefan Ashton - all of whom knocked it out of the park. So, onto some further important details on next week's excitement. THOSE WANTING TO STAY ON 41 Build 41 savegames clearly will not be compatible with Build 42. If you are a Build 41 player who wants to minimise disruption on the 42 launch, or a server owner / online player who wants to continue on Build 41, then there is already a beta channel for you (and your players) to move over to before the event. To do so: Right-click PZ in your Steam library. Select "Properties". Under "Game Versions & Betas" select "legacy41". {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4460946/c1cb9282f98915e6d57f248b3e9edd1698fd368a.gif FOR THOSE WANTING TO FINISH AN UNSTABLE 42.19 GAME Due to additional content being added, existing saves on Unstable 42.19 will not be compatible with 42.20. To continue your Unstable game you can opt-in to the new “42.19” beta. To do so: Right-click PZ in your Steam library. Select "Properties". Under "Game Versions & Betas" select "42.19". 42.20 CONTENT We will be running a blog early next week to go over some of the new aspects that are being added into 42.20, which will be accompanied by an interview with our Art Director that MrAtomicDuck has recorded - in the same vein as the one he did with our Design Director Christian Allen. As mentioned previously, repeated here as not everyone reads every blog, the patch also addresses issues with: Character Spawns Controllers Meat yield from Butcher Hooks Vehicle Towing Zombie culling in MP GOING FORWARD Again, this is repeated information from our last blog - so apologies for any deja-vu - but it's important that everyone knows the plan. patches.title: NEXT STEPS
patches.content: {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4460946/9a177cd005d428d8ec51728a0dd1ad079cb89ba1.jpg Hello Survivors! It’s July 9th, something of a key date in PZ lore, so we felt it was a great time to check in with you to lay out our overall plans for the rest of the year. So pack up the car, fuel up the generator, and let’s get ready for a loot run! 42.20 Unstable Build 42.20 is in the testing phase, and it’s a big one, with a few yet-to-be-revealed surprises a big portion of the team has been designing and creating. We’ll announce the specifics once the update is complete, and are targeting a release later this summer. Additionally, Unstable players will want to be aware that we have also been addressing issues around the following: Character Spawns Controllers Meat yield from Butcher Hooks Vehicle Towing Zombie culling in MP Map chunk loading when driving in MP And loads more.. Due to a large content update, unfortunately 42.19 save games will not be transferable to 42.20. However, you have at least a few weeks before the release from this point to play out your games – and 42.19 will still be available on the ‘outdatedunstable’ branch if you choose. THE ROAD TO 42 STABLE AND BEYOND At this point we have identified 42.20 as the build candidate that will move to the Stable branch, and barring unforeseen circumstances, when it launches it will do so as the default launch option on Steam. The move to Stable marks an important milestone for Unstable beta players who have been dealing with save breakages from multiple updates, and likewise for mod authors to have a far less changeable platform to build upon. Of course, this will also introduce Build 42 to the broader community that doesn’t choose to opt-in to Unstable builds – and allow us to gather feedback from those players as well as from more uninterrupted longer-term playthroughs. Once all PZ players are on the Stable version, our current plans are as follows: After any necessary hot fixes are identified and released, we will begin working on a patch consisting of tweaks and adjustments based on player feedback – primarily aimed at the late game. patches.title: REINFORCING THE BARRICADES
patches.content: {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4460946/63746381a78ca3f6108bc4fc54c8de1897abe0f2.jpg Hello, Survivors! Today we are bringing you some news related to our localization process, along with a quick preview of the upcoming 42.19 Update! So throw some beef jerky into your fanny pack, fill up your canteen with whiskey, and let’s take a look: LOCALIZATION: A PIVOT Previously, TIS announced that Project Zomboid would be moving to external localization for Build 42 and beyond. However, after trying this process out and then mixing in many separate changes and recent improvements to our workflow, we believe that the extended future of both the game and community would be better served by returning to the community translation model that we had been so proud of up to and through Build 41. To explain our reasoning: In hindsight, one reason we initially put a halt on community translation is simply because our pipeline was too unwieldy and our processes weren’t good enough backstage to manage the data flow. Now, with coders experienced in this field who have worked with a very similar set-up on the Minecraft Java Edition, which provides support for 100 languages, we can supply a far more engaging, interactive and collaborative set-up to benefit the languages we intend to support – and those who were going to miss out on participating. In switching to an external localization team we realized that we were putting a decade’s worth of known and loved phrases, titles and terminology (including some that even the PZ team themselves were ignorant of) at a degree of risk. Through the full gamut of the game, modding, and localization the new PZ team leaders view community as vital and something we want to dive deeper into on all fronts - and not ignoring its history and how things have formerly come to be is a big part of this. Looking forward, the community translation model is a smoother and more organic way of supporting our style of development in terms of the way we run an Unstable beta, feature integration, and patching. For those working on the game, too, it’s less stop/start, allows for a constant dripfeed of edits, fixes and improvements in every update we make, and brings more flexibil...
